**My thinking as this farmer:**

I've been farming this land my whole life, same as my father before me. Around here in Quzhou, everyone does winter wheat then summer maize — that's just what the land is for. The soil is good flat ground, we have the irrigation wells, and I know how to do it. Trying something new and failing would be a disaster for my family.

I have about 12 mu total. I'll put all of it into the wheat-maize rotation like every year. My neighbor Li told me the seed station is still selling 济麦22 for wheat — it did well last year — so I'll buy that. For maize I'll get hybrid seeds,郑单958 or whatever the station has, because those outyield the old varieties by a lot and I know this from experience.

For fertilizer I put down a good base coat before planting and top-dress later. I probably use more nitrogen than I need to, but I'd rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose yield. I'll irrigate wheat three times — the pre-winter water is important, then at jointing, then heading. Maize I might only need once since July-August usually brings rain. I'll spray herbicide on both crops and watch for aphids on the wheat come spring.

I'll plough the wheat field in October before planting, but after wheat harvest I'll direct-seed the maize straight into the stubble — saves time and fuel.
